title: How Casey Adams turned a teen podcast into a network that funded a startup and launched Listener
summary: Casey Adams explains how he started a podcast at 17 to meet great people, learn, and create business opportunity, and how that network later funded Media Kits and led to Listener. He shares his cold-outreach framework for landing big guests and why founder-led media is a distribution channel.

principles.text: Judge the podcast by a simple checklist, not revenue: meet great people, learn from them, create business opportunity.
principles.quote: meet great people, learn from them, and create business opportunities.

principles.text: A show's network compounds into capital: most of his angel investors were past guests.
principles.quote: we had 37 angel investors and pretty much 90% of those investors were past guests from my podcast.

principles.text: Make cold outreach short, tied to what the person cares about right now, and respectful of their time.
principles.quote: figuring out what they care about, you know, he loves Robert Green, he's a friend of his, and you kind of the barrier kind of goes down

principles.text: Use mutual connections as social proof in the ask: name someone they know and like who has been on your show.
principles.quote: hey Rick Ross, I recently had your friend Robert Green on my podcast. It would be such an honor to have you on my show for 15 minutes to talk about your new book.

principles.text: Time pitches to why now: guests are most receptive when promoting a book, film, or cause.
principles.quote: you'll see a lot of these bigger creators or celebrities go on these podcast tours because they're talking about something specific that they care about at that time

principles.text: Don't fear rejection: send the ask anyway and expect far more no's than yeses.
principles.quote: I've probably had more nos or me messages that didn't respond than I've ever had received or the big guests that you've heard of
